description: Crypto and Privacy Village at DEF CON 24 explores applied cryptography, surveillance resistance, TLS inspection, PKI architecture, legal decryption battles, and usable security.

talks.title: Andrew Brandt
talks.teaser: Examining Blue Coat SSL Visibility appliances, inspecting how enterprise TLS interception works, certificates are handled, and privacy is impacted.

talks.title: Alisha Kloc
talks.teaser: Why traditional system and application logs fall short for forensic investigations, and how privacy-preserving telemetry enhances detection.

talks.title: Greg Norcie - My Usability Goes to 11 A Hackers Guide to Use
talks.teaser: A hacker guide to usable security and human factors in privacy tooling, examining why cryptographically sound software often fails users.

talks.title: Ladar Levison - Compelled Decryption: State of the Art in Doctrinal Perversity
talks.teaser: Lavabit founder Ladar Levison analyzes constitutional protections, legal precedents, and government attempts to compel cryptographic key disclosure.

talks.title: Nate Cardozo - Crypto State of the Law
talks.teaser: EFF Senior Staff Attorney Nate Cardozo provides a legal briefing on legislative battles, court rulings, and government backdoors targeting encryption.

talks.title: Mat Caughron, Trey Blalock - Revocation the Frailty of PKI
talks.teaser: Analyzing certificate revocation protocols including CRL and OCSP, exploring the systemic vulnerabilities and privacy leaks undermining public PKI.

talks.title: David Wong - How to Backdoor Diffie-Hellman
talks.teaser: Cryptographer David Wong demonstrates how to construct cryptographic backdoors into Diffie-Hellman key exchanges using malicious prime selection.

talks.title: Panel
talks.teaser: A panel discussion exploring privacy, open-source intelligence gathering, and ethical dilemmas encountered when detecting deception and infidelity.
